segments.he: א' גדול מאנ"ש שביזו אותו והחריש על בזיונו ואמרו לו מדוע אתה שותק כבוד התורה. ענה ואמר תאמינו לי שבדיבור א' יכולתי להשתיקו אך מפני זה שתקתי ולא עניתי מפני כבוד התורה. כי מתחלה מתחיל בכבוד התורה ואח"כ סיים בכבוד עצמו ע"כ שיתקבל ומוותר על כבוד התורה שלו. עס פייבט זיך אן בכבוד התורה אין לאזטי זיך אוס בכבוד עצמו".
segments.en:
Reb Natan's custom during the Three Weeks was to recite the kinos [lamentations] with tallis and tefillin. And on the eve of Tisha B'Av from midday he would close himself in a deep cellar and remain there locked in weeping, wailing, and strange voices until past midday of Tisha B'Av itself — and this was his custom every year after Rabbainu's passing. He could not cool his mind until he would see Rabbainu. And the Rav Reb Shmuel Yitzchak of Tcheryn — one of the greatest disciples of Rabbainu — was once with Reb Natan on Tisha B'Av and witnessed his custom as described. When Reb Natan emerged from the cellar, his face full of hope, Reb Shmuel Yitzchak was struck at his appearance and said [words of praise for Rabbainu] — adding that he had not known Rabbainu's greatness as well until that very year.

And Reb Nachman of Tulchin on Tisha B'Av — at night and through the day until midday — would not speak a single word with any person and would not study Midrash with the congregation, as was the custom of the day — for he said that Tisha B'Av is like a mourner, G-d preserve us, and a mourner is forbidden to speak.

And the holy Rav of Berdichev would wear his shtreiml on Erev Tisha B'Av — and wait near the time of nightfall, hoping that Mashiach would come so he could go out to greet him. When nightfall arrived and Mashiach had not come, he would throw off those garments and cast himself to the ground, weeping and crying: "May Hashem send us our righteous Mashiach speedily, kain yehi ratzon."

I heard: after Rabbainu's passing, on the first Shabbos, the disciples of Rabbainu were gathered in Rabbainu's house. Reb Yudel said he would sit in Rabbainu's chair — because he had inherited Rabbainu's shtreiml. And other disciples answered him. Then Moharan'as arose and said that he would sit in the chair — because he had inherited the mochin [higher mind] of Rabbainu. For tefillin is mochin — and once Rabbainu had been traveling and asked Moharan'as for his Rabbainu Tam tefillin, wore them, and returned them. Moharan'as sat in the chair and began to sing Azamer Bishvachin with great arousal. And the holy Magid of Terhovitsa leaped from the table and said with burning arousal: "I thought it was Reb Noson — but now I see it is Rabbainu himself!" And the essential root of the controversy of the Rabbi of Savran against Reb Noson was that Moharan'as bound himself with great self-sacrifice so that Rabbainu's matter should endure for all generations — and he would not allow the Rabbi of Savran to marry Idel the daughter of Rabbainu, for this would have been a great harm to Rabbainu's legacy. And when the match was being discussed, Idel asked the Rabbi of Savran: "I have heard you dispute with my father." He replied: "Not with your father — only with his disciple [Moharan'as], who said your father is as great as Moshe Rabbainu." She replied: "What is the difference? Moshe Rabbainu brought down the Torah — and my father brings people to fulfill it." And the match was not completed, for Moharan'as did not agree.

And so it was also at the great Shavuos at Moharan'as's — with eighty guests plus the townsfolk, and very great arousal. And Moharan'as himself said about that Shavuos that it should be called "the Great Shavuos" — and one must be careful at such a great Shavuos not to make the Golden Calf, for at the giving of the Torah too there was a great Shavuos and afterward they made the Golden Calf. And the Magid of Terhovitsa said there too that he thought it was Moharan'as — but in the end saw it was Rabbainu himself. And he said: if he had known this, he would not have traveled to Eretz Yisroel and would have stayed with him.
